text:
lee.kim: Heads up — we're onboarding a 12-node A100 GPU pool in sa-east-1 next week and I need a public IP headroom / VPC quota bump.

maria.gonzalez: what counts as headroom here? how many EIPs do we need attached vs spare? :thinking_face:

lee.kim: planning details: 12 nodes, each node will host multiple pods with hostNetwork=false so we need one ENI per node for node-level services + one Elastic IP per NATed node for cross-region callbacks. also want capacity for rolling canaries. requesting extras for scale and safety.

sam.tan: can we avoid 12 EIPs by using NAT Gateway + SNAT? NAT gw costs are annoying but might be cheaper than holding many EIPs.

lee.kim: we considered NAT but vendor callbacks require stable public addresses per node (they do IP allowlisting). reassigning via NAT would break that.

maria.gonzalez: ok put numbers? I'll draft the cloud support justification.

lee.kim: requested quotas:```
- Elastic IPs (standard): +48 (current 5 -> request 53)
- EC2 ENI limit per region: +60
- VPC per account: +2 (we need an extra VPC for staging-prod isolation)
- IPv4 addresses in subnet (secondary IPs): increase /24 -> /22 planned for each dedicated subnet
- Enable/confirm IPv6 for the VPC (we want GCP-like dual-stack later)
```
This gives us ~4 spare EIPs for failover and canary pools.

infra-bot: cloud-support ticket created: CASE-9854321 — "EIP/ENI/VPC quota increase for sa-east-1 GPU onboarding". ETA initial response: 24-48h. Assigned to cloud-support.

cloud-support: thanks, we have the ticket. Quick clarifying Qs: can you provide an IP allowlist example from the vendor and the timeline for when addresses must be available? Also please confirm whether EIPs will be attached continuously or can be allocated on-demand during deploys.

lee.kim: vendor allowlist example: 52.210.14.0/28, 52.210.18.32/29 (they only accept specific /28-/29 blocks, hence per-node static EIPs). Need them by 2026-04-01 for staged rollout. EIPs will be attached continuously per node.

maria.gonzalez: adding cost justification: the per-EIP hourly idle charge is acceptable compared to rework risk and vendor SLA penalties. Also call out alternative ops: move vendor allowlisting to an ALB in front of our nodes if they agree.

sam.tan: from infra side, also request quota bump for "Network interfaces per ENI"? (we hit issues when pods create many secondary IPs). Propose secondary IP limit increase to 50 per ENI.

lee.kim: adding that to the ticket now.

infra-bot: CASE-9854321 updated: added ENI secondary IPs +50, updated justification, uploaded architecture diagram (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/sa-east-gpu-networking.png).

cloud-support: accepted the justification, submitting backend change. Preliminary approval for ENI and VPC changes, EIP increase pending provider confirmation.

maria.gonzalez: thanks — once EIPs are approved we should also reserve a small /28 in the subnet for control-plane services.

sam.tan: FYI I've added a Terraform patch to allocate the larger subnet and annotate resources for cost tracking. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/terra/pulls/2114

lee.kim: great. I'll keep tracking CASE-9854321 and ping if we don't see an update in 36h. :thumbsup:
